worked_example.task_and_answer: Scalar link U_xy=i sends psi_y=2 to2i in frame x; inverse -i restores2. A2x2 link diag(i,-i) sends(1,2) to(i,-2i), norm squared5; conjugate transpose restores input.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: U_xy=-i sends psi_y=1+i to1-i; inverse i restores1+i, norm squared2. For diag(-1, i), input(2,1) gives(-2, i), norm squared5 and inverse diag(-1,-i) restores.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: U_xy and U_yx cannot be silently exchanged. With a unitary link U_yx=U_xy dagger; it maps the other direction.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Introduce normalized lift maps and orthogonal label spaces, then finite Fourier channels with complex adjoints. Specify a synthetic nine-translation model, keeping the missing source L/P_v definitions separate. Include the Weyl supplement and rank bridge.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic L={(a, b,0):a, b=0,1,2}; P_v delta_x=delta_(x+v). Set V f=(1/3)sum_v P_v f tensor |v>. Orthogonal labels give V dagger V=(1/9)sum P_v dagger P_v=I27. A unit delta input gives nine amplitudes 1/3 and norm 1.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Input 2 delta_(1,0,0) gives nine amplitudes 2/3 and norm squared 4; V dagger V restores it. Separately use F_jk=omega^(jk)/sqrt(3): F e0=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3), F e1=(1, omega, omega^2)/sqrt(3), and F dagger reverses both.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Using 27 unitary translations with prefactor 1/3 gives norm-squared factor 3, not 1. The source all-lifts claim requires its exact L and operators; AUD-009 records missing objects. This nine-label model is explicitly a classroom analogue.

supplemental_exercises.explanation: Define omega=(-1+i sqrt(3))/2, omega^3=1 and 1+omega+omega^2=0. With P e_j=e_(j+1 modulo 3), D=diag(1, omega, omega^2), set B_ab=D^a P^b. Teach trace and Hermitian orthogonality before extracting coefficients.
supplemental_exercises.worked_task_and_answer: DP=omega PD and Tr(B_ab dagger B_cd)=3 delta_ac delta_bd. For Y=I+2P-D^2 P, y_ab=Tr(B_ab dagger Y)/3 gives y00=1, y01=2, y21=-1 and all six other coefficients zero. Rebuild Y from all nine coordinates.
supplemental_exercises.practice_task_and_answer: For Y=2I+D-P^2, y00=2, y10=1, y02=-1 and all others zero. Direct Y has diagonal (3,2+omega,2+omega^2) and -1 at positions (0,1),(1,2),(2,0). Check each trace coefficient and entrywise reconstruction; retain zeros.
supplemental_exercises.diagnostic_task_and_answer: A basis decomposition represents a supplied Y; it does not select physical Y. Swapping D/P order changes phases, so retain the exact basis and trace convention.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Preserve EA-20-E07-3. Teach column independence through linear equations, then distinguish carrier dimension, product-label count and projector image rank. Retain the complement of every projection.

worked_example.task_and_answer: C20-RANK-EX1: P=[[1/2,1/2,0],[1/2,1/2,0],[0,0,1]]. P^2=P; the first two columns coincide and the third is independent, so rank is 2 in dimension 3. P(2,0,3)=(1,1,3); complement=(1,-1,0).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: C20-RANK-P1: P(4,2,-1)=(3,3,-1), complement=(1,-1,0), and their sum restores the input. A 2-by-3 label table has six entries. I2 tensor I3 tensor diag(1,0) acts in dimension 12 with rank 6.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: C20-RANK-D1: diag(1,0,0) has rank 1, not 3. A label count does not establish projector rank without its independent image basis.

worked_example.task_and_answer: The image basis has 16 internal choices, 3 family choices and 1 history choice: rank 48. Each family restriction has 16 internal states and one history coordinate. The stated family/history occupation label (1,1,1) is not a measured density.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: The toy I2 tensor I3 tensor q1 has rank 6, two internal states per family. Finite history q3=0 gives rank 0. A rank-2 history factor would give rank 96 in the 16-by-3 product, showing why rank(q_n)=1 matters.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: I3 makes this declared projector uniform across labels. It does not by itself prove that physical states occupy its image. Retain the SA-20 claim, guard and correction records.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Separate family labels from numerical masses, mixing and supplied matrix coefficients. Teach block elimination with full reconstruction and an explicit E=0 branch; keep the Weyl basis separate from choosing physical coefficients.

worked_example.task_and_answer: A three-family carrier does not determine a Yukawa matrix. For synthetic K=[[2,1],[1,3]], s=(5,7), E=3, Schur=5/3, reduced source=8/3, u=8/5 and w=9/5. Both original equations hold; det K=5.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: K=[[3,1],[2,2]], s=(7,8) gives E=2, Schur=2, reduced source=3, u=3/2, w=5/2 and det K=4. With E=0, use K=[[1,1],[1,0]], s=(3,1): solve the original equations to get u=1, w=2 without dividing by E.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Elimination from an intermediate equation does not authorize forgetting w. Preserve all zero Weyl coordinates, singular branches, coefficient inputs and physical-occupation premises.

supplemental_exercises.explanation: For A u+B w=sU and C u+E w=sW, invertible E permits w=E^-1(sW-Cu), Schur S=A-BE^-1C and reduced source r=sU-BE^-1sW. Solve S u=r only if its own inverse exists. Keep both original equations.
supplemental_exercises.practice_task_and_answer: K=[[3,1],[2,2]], s=(7,8) gives S=2, r=3, u=3/2, w=5/2. Then 3u+w=7,2u+2w=8 and det K=4. For E=0, K=[[1,1],[1,0]], s=(3,1), directly solve u=1, w=2; K is invertible even though E is not.
supplemental_exercises.diagnostic_task_and_answer: Singular E or S falls outside the corresponding inverse formula. Retain compatibility or free coordinates, or solve the full system. Never erase w or treat division by zero as a branch solution.
